claims.claim: Plate tectonics explains that Earth’s outer rigid shell is divided into plates that move relative to one another.
The lithosphere includes crust and stiff upper mantle and moves over a softer mantle layer called the asthenosphere.
Ocean-floor mapping, magnetic reversals, seafloor spreading, and distributions of earthquakes and volcanoes helped establish plate-tectonic theory.
New oceanic crust at a mid-ocean ridge is young and becomes older away from the ridge; alternating magnetic stripes parallel to ridges record field reversals and support seafloor spreading.
Plate tectonics is a unifying geological model because broad patterns of mountains, earthquakes, volcanoes, shorelines, and ocean basins are associated with moving plates and their interactions.
